claim: MAC's Grand-Hornu opens Tuesday-Sunday 10am-6pm; tickets €10 adults, €6 reduced, free under 6 and on the first Sunday of each month; same-day train ticket to Mons/Saint-Ghislain gives free site access
quote: Tuesday to Sunday, 10am to 6pm. Regular admission: €10. Reduced rate: €6 (seniors 60+, students). Free on the first Sunday of the month. Same-day train tickets to Mons or Saint-Ghislain receive complimentary site access.

claim: MAC's reopens 14 June 2026 with three new exhibitions: Lucia Bru 'Aux choses mêmes' (until 1 Nov 2026), 'Ravi de te connaître: Gifts to the Museum' (until 16 Aug 2026), and 'Le Regard éloigné: A Selection from the Collection' (until 16 Aug 2026)
quote: Lucia Bru: Aux choses mêmes — June 14, 2026 – November 1, 2026. Ravi de te connaître: Gifts to the Museum — June 14, 2026 – August 16, 2026. Le Regard éloigné: A Selection from the Collection — June 14, 2026 – August 16, 2026.

claim: CID at Grand-Hornu runs 'Memo. Remembering the Futures' from 29 March to 30 August 2026, bringing together international artists and designers around loss and memory
quote: Running from March 29 to August 30, 2026, 'Memo. Remembering the Futures' brings together a constellation of international artists and designers to confront one of the defining anxieties of our era.

claim: CID's preceding exhibition Patricia Urquiola 'Meta-Morphosa' runs 14 December 2025 to 26 April 2026, framed as an 'exhibition-manifesto' on the mutability of contemporary design
quote: Patricia Urquiola: Meta-Morphosa runs from December 14, 2025 through April 26, 2026. Positioned as an 'exhibition-manifesto,' the show analyzes the mutability of contemporary design.

claim: Grand-Hornu is a neoclassical former colliery built 1810-1830 by industrialist Henri De Gorge to architect Bruno Renard's designs, comprising workshops, a 450-house workers' coron and the De Gorge château across 10,000 m² of buildings on a 3.5-ha park
quote: The Grand-Hornu, an old industrial coal mining complex from the Industrial Revolution, was built on the initiative of Henri De Gorge by architect Bruno Renard. The site covers 10,000 m² of built structures on 3.5 hectares of park.

claim: Grand-Hornu and Bois-du-Luc were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2012 as part of the 'Major Mining Sites of Wallonia' serial property with Bois du Cazier and Blegny-Mine, forming a 170 km strip of the best-preserved 19th- and 20th-century Belgian coal-mining sites
quote: The four sites of the property form a strip 170 km long by 3–15 km wide, crossing Belgium from east to west, consisting of the best-preserved 19th- and 20th-century coal-mining sites of the country.

claim: Bois-du-Luc Museum of Mining and Sustainable Development is at 2b rue Saint-Patrice, 7110 La Louvière; open Tue-Fri 10-17h year-round and weekends/holidays 10-18h April-September; free parking, E19/E42 exit 21 (Le Rœulx)
quote: Adresse: 2b rue Saint Patrice, 7110 La Louvière. Mardi-vendredi 10h-17h. Weekends et jours fériés d'avril à septembre 10h-18h. Par voiture: E19/E42, sortie 21 (Le Rœulx). Parking gratuit.

claim: Bois-du-Luc free visit costs €9 adults, €8 seniors, €6 students/under-18 (free under 6); guided tours Sunday 10:30 and 15:00 from 1 April to 30 September at €12 adults; one of Europe's oldest collieries with buildings 1838-1909
quote: Visite libre: adultes 9€, 60+ 8€, étudiants et enfants (<18) 6€. Visite guidée dimanche à 10h30 et 15h du 1/04 au 30/09: adultes 12€.

claim: Cruises on the historic Canal du Centre depart Strépy-Thieu (Rue Raymond Cordier 50, 7070 Thieu) Wed-Sun, 10am and 2pm, April-October; 2h30 duration; €18 adults, €15 teens/seniors, €12 children 4-12; includes locks, lifts, machine-room tour and return by train
quote: Cruises operate Wednesday to Sunday, April 2 through October 31, with departures at 10 a.m. and 2 p.m. Duration: two hours and thirty minutes. Adults: €18, Teens (13-18) & Seniors (60+): €15, Children (4-12): €12. Includes passage through locks, elevators, movable bridges, plus a tour of the machine room.

claim: Strépy-Thieu interior visit (interpretation centre and film) runs 22 February to 2 November, daily except Mondays 10am-6pm with last entry 16:45; tickets €10 adults, €8 seniors/students, €5.50 children 4-12, free under 4
quote: Du 22 février au 2 novembre, tous les jours sauf le lundi, de 10h à 18h, dernière visite à 16h45. Adultes 10€, 60+ et étudiants 8€, enfants 4-12 ans 5,50€, 0-3 ans gratuit.

claim: The Strépy-Thieu funicular boat lift interpretation centre (inaugurated March 2019) features the machine room, panoramic view, animated scale models, interactive games and a film on construction and operation; bookings via voiesdeau.hainaut.be
quote: The interpretation centre was inaugurated in March 2019 and features an impressive machinery room, a superb panorama of the site and the region, animated scale models, interactive games and a movie about the lift's construction and operation.

claim: The four hydraulic boat lifts on the historic Canal du Centre at La Louvière and Le Roeulx were inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage in 1998; designed by English engineer Edwin Clark, they are the only hydraulic boat lifts in the world still working in their original 19th-century condition
quote: The Four Lifts on the Canal du Centre and their Environs, La Louvière and Le Roeulx (Hainaut). Of the eight hydraulic boat-lifts built at the end of the 19th and beginning of the 20th century, the only ones in the world which still exist in their original working condition are these four lifts on the Canal du Centre.

claim: Road distance from Baudour to Strépy-Bracquegnies (location of historic Canal du Centre lifts and ~3 km from Strépy-Thieu) is 25 km
quote: 25 Km - Distance entre Baudour et 7110 Strépy-Bracquegnies.

claim: Road distance Baudour to La Louvière (which administratively includes Houdeng-Aimeries, site of Bois-du-Luc) is ~31 km, about 22 minutes by car
quote: The road distance is 19.2 miles (approximately 31 km). It takes approximately 22 minutes to drive from Baudour to La Louvière.
